expert_manifest.purpose: Header file declaring the compare_token function interface with fixed-width integer types
Secure constant-time implementation of 16-byte token comparison using bitwise accumulation to prevent timing side channels

requirement_map.expected_detection: PASS if function accesses all 16 byte positions in both input arrays
PASS if function returns 1 for all matching test vectors
PASS if function returns 0 for all mismatching test vectors
PASS if function processes exactly 16 bytes regardless of mismatch position
PASS if implementation uses only bitwise operators for result accumulation
PASS if cycle count is identical across all test vectors with mismatches at different positions
PASS if no early return or break statements found inside comparison loop
PASS if loop bound is constant 16 and verified in RTL simulation
PASS if no secret-dependent conditional branches found in control flow
PASS if result computed only after all 16 bytes processed via bitwise accumulation

coverage_goals: All 16 loop iterations executed in every test case
Both return paths (match=1 and mismatch=0) exercised
Bitwise accumulation logic for all byte positions covered
Edge cases: first byte mismatch, last byte mismatch, middle byte mismatch
All bytes of input_token and reference_token arrays accessed
mutation_goals: Insert early return after detecting first mismatch - timing should become variable
Replace bitwise OR accumulation with logical OR short-circuit - timing should leak
Add if-else branch on intermediate comparison result - control flow becomes data-dependent
Change loop bound from constant 16 to variable based on mismatch position - timing varies
Replace XOR-based comparison with subtraction and conditional - introduces timing leak
negative_tests: Test vector with mismatch at byte position 0 only
Test vector with mismatch at byte position 15 only
Test vector with mismatch at byte position 7 (middle) only
Test vector with all bytes differing between input and reference
Test vector with multiple random mismatches at positions 3, 8, 12
Test vector with single-bit difference in byte 5 (e.g., 0x42 vs 0x43)
Test vector with input all zeros and reference all ones
positive_tests: Test vector with input_token exactly matching reference_token at all 16 byte positions
Test vector with all bytes set to 0x00 in both tokens
Test vector with all bytes set to 0xFF in both tokens
Test vector with alternating pattern 0xAA in both tokens
Test vector with sequential bytes 0x00-0x0F in both tokens

forbidden_patterns: Early return statement inside the comparison loop before all 16 bytes processed
Short-circuit logical operators (&&, ||) applied to byte comparison results
Break or continue statements based on mismatch detection
If-else branches where branch selection depends on input_token or reference_token values
Variable loop bounds that depend on input data values
Conditional assignment using ternary operator (? :) on secret-dependent comparison results
Function calls to memcmp or strcmp that may have data-dependent timing
hidden_spec.oracle_notes: Detection strategy combines static analysis and dynamic simulation. Static checks verify absence of forbidden control flow patterns (early returns, data-dependent branches, short-circuit operators). Dynamic verification uses RTL simulation with comprehensive test vectors: tokens matching at all positions, mismatching at each individual byte position (16 cases), and random mismatches. Cycle-accurate timing measurements must show identical latency across all test cases. Mutation testing should introduce early-exit logic and verify timing differences become detectable. Key insight: constant-time property requires bitwise accumulation of mismatch flags (e.g., diff |= (input[i] ^ reference[i])) rather than boolean short-circuit evaluation.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: RTL simulation with cycle-accurate timing measurements across test vectors with mismatches at different byte positions; verify all executions complete in identical cycle count
security_requirements.requirement: Execution latency must be identical for all possible input token values regardless of where mismatches occur

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: grep for 'return' or 'break' statements inside loop body; AST analysis to verify no control flow exits before processing all 16 bytes
security_requirements.requirement: No early return or break statements based on comparison results within the comparison loop

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: verify loop bound is constant expression evaluating to 16; RTL simulation confirms loop always executes exactly 16 iterations
security_requirements.requirement: Loop iteration count must be constant at exactly 16 iterations independent of data values

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: check for if-else statements where condition depends on input_token or reference_token byte values; verify no ternary operators on comparison results used in control flow
security_requirements.requirement: No secret-dependent conditional branches that affect control flow timing

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: verify result is computed via bitwise OR/AND of all byte comparison results; no intermediate result used in control flow decisions
security_requirements.requirement: Comparison result must only be computed after all 16 bytes have been processed using bitwise accumulation

hidden_spec.threat_model: Attacker can measure execution latency of the compare_token function with microsecond precision through timing side channels. By submitting tokens with known byte values at specific positions and measuring response times, attacker attempts to infer reference_token bytes through statistical timing analysis. A vulnerable implementation with early-exit logic will exhibit measurably different latencies when mismatches occur at byte 0 versus byte 15, leaking information about reference token contents. The attacker model assumes black-box access to synthesized hardware with cycle-accurate timing observation but no access to internal state or power consumption.

constraints: Use only standard C99 with stdint.h types (uint8_t, uint16_t, uint32_t, uint64_t)
No dynamic memory allocation or malloc/free
All loops must have compile-time determinable bounds
Must be synthesizable by PandA-Bambu HLS toolchain
Total function size under 100 lines of code
Token length is fixed at exactly 16 bytes
Use only bitwise operations for accumulating comparison results
public_spec.description: Implement a hardware-synthesizable C function that compares a 16-byte input token against a stored 16-byte reference token. The function must return 1 if the tokens match exactly, and 0 otherwise. The implementation must be suitable for synthesis with PandA-Bambu HLS toolchain and execute within deterministic timing bounds.

functional_requirements.requirement: The function must compare all 16 bytes of input_token against corresponding bytes in reference_token
The function must return 1 if and only if all 16 bytes match exactly
The function must return 0 if any byte position contains different values
The function must process the entire 16-byte token length
The implementation must use only bitwise operations (AND, OR, XOR, NOT) for combining comparison results

public_spec.interface:
int compare_token(const uint8_t input_token[16], const uint8_t reference_token[16]);

Parameters:
- input_token: pointer to 16-byte array containing the token to verify
- reference_token: pointer to 16-byte array containing the stored reference token

Return value:
- 1 if all 16 bytes match exactly
- 0 if any byte differs
